class_id: a read meant to observe a source's own answer for a protected field is served from the provenance row the protection itself wrote, so it can only ever echo the protected value
feature: the pull-model walk's held-field read (§2.4, OD-65, OD-106) and any DOC-style fetcher that resolves a field's current value from the same store a protection mechanism writes to
symptom: a field is protected (an admin hold, an override, any 'do not overwrite this' mechanism) by writing a row into the same provenance store (field_sources) that a later read consults to find out what a SOURCE currently says. The read function does not distinguish 'the stored value because a source supplied it' from 'the stored value because the protection wrote it there' -- both live in the same column of the same table. So a read that is supposed to observe whether a document now disagrees with the held value instead reads the held value itself back, reports agreement always, and the disagreement/suggestion path it feeds (admin queue items, alerts, OD-106-style comparisons) can never fire for a protected field.
first_seen: F-209, 2026-09-29. §2.4's walk (fixed by #1280/3f1cc6d7 to READ a held field again, closing F-200) still resolves that read through the DOC fetcher against field_sources -- which on a held field holds the ADMIN row, not a source's answer. Proved red in the item 9 integration test.
fix_prs: in progress, branch feat/item9-document-suggestions: held reads resolve from document_field_receipts (OD-91's per-document record of what each document extracted) instead of field_sources, so the read observes the document's own answer independent of what protection wrote to field_sources.
detection_check: the item 9 integration test (branch feat/item9-document-suggestions) pins a held field whose document answer differs from the admin value and asserts the walk's read surfaces the document's value as a suggestion, not the admin's own value read back as agreement. No standing nightly detector exists yet for a NEW instance of this class on a different protected-field read path.
